comment: Mutation testing for the CODE FIX PROVIDERS. A fourth config rather than entries in stryker-config.json because Stryker mutates ONE project per run, and this is a different project (DwarfMapper.CodeFixes.csproj). WHY THIS LEG EXISTS (round 27): a scope audit measured that only 15.3 % of src/ sits inside any leg's 'mutate' globs, and singled this project out -- 88.8 % LINE coverage with 0 % mutation coverage, precisely the combination mutation testing exists to interrogate, because it describes code thoroughly EXECUTED by tests that may assert nothing about it. It is also the most literally user-facing code in the repository: an analyzer reports a problem and these rewrite the consumer's own source to fix it, so a fix that emits subtly wrong code is worse than one that fails loudly. FIRST MEASUREMENT 2026-08-26: 52.54 % (93 detected of 177 scoreable; 55 survived, 29 uncovered). The prediction held -- barely half the mutants detected in code that is 88.8 % executed. AFTER THE KILL PROGRAM, same day, four batches, whole suite, 12 logical cores, Release build via scripts/gate-checks.ps1: score 87.01 % (154 detected of 177 -- 154 killed, 0 timeout; 19 survived, 4 uncovered), 6 min 20 s wall-clock. break is that score floored to 87, low tracks break, high sits above it. Per provider: ResolveExplicitOnlyMember 90.3 %, RestateBaseConfiguration 87.6 %, AddMapIgnore 87.5 %, AddReverseMapInverse 80.0 %. WHAT THE 61 KILLS WERE ABOUT. Three themes, none of them 'more tests of the happy path'. (1) THE REFUSALS: every provider declines to offer a fix when its inputs are unusable -- a dotted member, an empty or absent diagnostic property, a location outside the syntax the fix rewrites -- and not one refusal was exercised, because the generator only ever produces the shapes that succeed. Reaching them needed SYNTHETIC diagnostics built with a chosen property bag and location. (2) WHAT THE USER SEES: action titles and equivalence keys. A blanked title is not a crash; it is an empty entry in the lightbulb, and ResolveExplicitOnlyMember offers two actions that differ only by their text. (3) SYNTAX A COMPILER WOULD HAVE REJECTED: a code fix reads syntax, not a compiled model, so `[MapIgnore<T>]` with no argument list and `[MapProperty<S,T>(Use = ...)]` with only named arguments are legal things to type. Reading the arguments without checking for their absence throws inside the user's lightbulb. EVERY REMAINING UNDETECTED MUTANT IS DISPOSITIONED -- 22 proven-equivalent and 1 probably-equivalent, with the case analysis for each in Issues/ledgers/codefixes-mutation-survivors.md and the machine-readable rows in Issues/ledgers/equivalent-mutants.md. rawCeiling is 87.57 %, so the measured 87.01 % sits one probably-equivalent mutant below the highest score this leg can honestly reach. ROUND 30 RE-MEASURE (2026-09-15, StrykerOutput/2026-09-15.18-27-07, clean tree at 7f96555): 87.15 % (156 of 179 -- 19 survived, 4 uncovered), rawCeiling (179 - 22) / 179 = 87.70 %; break stays 87. The RestateBase refactor (caef954) removed three killed mutants on changed lines and added five, and 7f96555 killed the one new survivor; the 23 undetected are still exactly the 23 ledger rows. Correction to caef954's own mutation claim: Issues/ledgers/round30-ledger.md. RE-MEASURED AGAIN the same day after 48213d0 removed the unreachable `?? classDecl` trivia fallback and retired the leg's one probably-equivalent row (StrykerOutput/2026-09-15.18-55-18): 87.64 % (156 of 178 -- 18 survived, 4 uncovered) = rawCeiling (178 - 22) / 178. Every undetected mutant is now a proven row, so this is the leg's honest ceiling; break stays 87. NOTE -- raise break only by killing survivors, never by re-measuring on a lucky run; the floor moves in the same commit as the kills that earned it. NOTE -- the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.CodeFixes, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard and returned 177 for this run. NOTE -- all four providers are listed explicitly rather than globbed with '**/*.cs', so adding a fifth is a deliberate act that shows up in review; the three sibling configs follow the same convention. ROUND 29 T2.3 ADDED A FIFTH PROVIDER, ConvertToRecordStructCodeFixProvider.cs (the DWARF103 transitive rewrite, 559 lines), AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED HERE YET -- measured, not assumed. Adding it and running the leg on 2026-09-06 gave 79.24 % (449 mutants created, 230 tested: 187 killed, 43 survived, 6 uncovered), which CRASHES this break. Two facts from that run decide it. First, 26 of the 43 survivors are in the new file and roughly half are provably equivalent -- three ConfigureAwait(false) flips, the two `converted.Add` lines that add the same symbol for a non-generic type, `Short`'s strip-the-'T:' branch that is a no-op for any namespaced id -- so even a complete kill program over THE MUTANTS THAT RAN lands near 85 %, BELOW this break -- and that figure is not itself a ceiling, because safe mode had truncated the set (next sentence). The raw ceiling moves either way, and re-pinning it needs the per-mutant case analysis Issues/ledgers/codefixes-mutation-survivors.md holds for the existing 23, not a lowered number. Second, Stryker's safe mode removed EVERY mutation in `Convert` and `ObliviousNestedMembers` -- the two methods that do the rewrite -- because two mutants there hit CS0165 and CS1503, so that run scored the new file on its periphery and would have said almost nothing about the code that edits a consumer's source. Lowering break to fit an unfinished leg would erode the gate the kill program earned; listing the file without the kill program would fail the nightly build. The debt is recorded instead, in Issues/round27/AUDIT-mutation-scope.md's table, where the scan pins it EXACTLY and it cannot rot: DwarfMapper.CodeFixes reads 4 of 5 files and 53.2 %, not 100 %. NOTE -- there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key; see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement showing such a list is inert here. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-26 (StrykerOutput/2026-09-26.12-14-29, clean tree at 5cc0491): score 87.64 % (156 detected of 178 scoreable), IDENTICAL to the 2026-09-15 figure, so no threshold moves. Run because the pin was stale in PROVENANCE even though it turned out current in value: the 2026-09-15 measurement was taken on the 48213d0 tree at 18:55, and two commits touching this assembly landed the same evening at 20:10 and 20:13 - one of them a behaviour fix (a DWARF103 handle without its T: prefix refused at registration rather than offered as a no-op). A floor measured before a behaviour change describes the wrong code even when the number happens to agree, so this records that it was checked rather than assumed. The leg remains AT its ceiling: 18 survivors plus 4 NoCoverage is 22 undetected against 22 proven-equivalent rows.
